full_judgment: 10. On a careful scrutiny of the documentary and oral evidence on record we find nothing to differ from the finding and observation of the trial Court about the genuineness of the disputed power of attorney Ext. 1(A) and exchange of the suit property. Moreover, according to the principles laid down in the case law reported in 10 D.L.R. page 1, Privy Council, K.M. Perera Vs. H.G. Martin Dias with the observation of Lord Denning and the case law reported in 36 D.L.R.(AD) Page 52 Md. Badruddin Khan Vs. Bangladesh and others in which the Appellate Division of Bangladesh Supreme Court observed that trial Court's findings should not be easily disturbed as a matter of course and before reversing the findings and decisions of the trial Court, the Appellate Court should think twice or more than twice. We do not find any error of law or of facts in the impugned judgment and decree delivered by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd court, Jhenidah. Moreover, in a Civil Matter, all the facts alleged by plaintiff. need not be proved strictly in view of the decision in the case of Jahed Ali Mondal Vs. Jamini Kanta Dey reported in 7 BLD(AD)page 156 and the burden of proof is lightened by presumption, admission and estoppel in view of this case law. It appears that the plaintiffs-respondents have discharged their primary onus to prove the genuineness of the disputed power of attorney Ext. 1(A). The six Govt. rent receipts Ext. 1 (d) upto 1(i) show that the kabala deed dated 13.2.64 executed by Samapada Biswas in favour of Santosh Kumar has been acted upon and the defendant appellants did not take any step for proving possession of the contesting defendants by producing any Govt. rent receipts along with the documentary evidence from Ext. 'A' upto Ext. (J).
